newsitem.title: UK: United News rebounds after Blenheim move.
newsitem.headline: United News rebounds after Blenheim move.

text.p: Shares in United News & Media Plc bounced higher on Tuesday after an early setback, with United's agreed bid for Blenheim seen complementing its existing businesses and priced at the low end of expectations.
By 0747 GMT United shares were up 23p at 676-1/2, after initially dropping some 8p on confirmation of the long-awaited bid, while Blenheim was up 23p at 496-1/2.

"Blenheim is complementary to United and it benefits its earnings and cash flow," said Anthony de Larrinaga, analyst at Panmure Gordon. "It is a nice business and there are not many like it around. And they have got it at a nice price."

"The market has every reason to like it," de Larrinaga said. "It is not ultra cheap but they were never going to get it ultra cheap. It is a good deal for both parties and is at the bottom end of the level we knew was acceptable to the Blenheim board."
The only remaining uncertainty after today's statement was over the 15 percent stake owned in Blenheim by Dutch publisher VNU, but VNU said it would not make a counter bid for Blenheim.
Yet analysts also pointed out the Blenheim bid may be a relatively minor aspect of developments going on at United News since its merger with MAI.
"Our figures suggest Blenheim should be earnings enhancing in the first full year, which is always a good sign," said another analyst who asked not to be named.

"But Blenheim is a bit of a side show, the real story is how they utilise all the restructuring provisions they have set up. There is a lot of restructuring still to come." -- David Holmes, London Newsroom +44 171 542 5106
